description: Colour literals intentionally left in the dashboard / admin JSX files owned by WS6 (contract 10.4 rule 5). ws6-js-scan.test.js fails on any literal in an owned, themed file that is neither a black shadow (X6) nor listed here with the exact occurrence count. W6-* ids are WS6-local categories that the contract exception list (X1-X13) does not cover.

legend.X1: Email HTML / customer email preview (contract X1): sent artifacts and the white wrapper around the preview document stay light.
legend.X2: Briefs, digests, published artifacts and every srcDoc iframe (contract X2), plus the X-post preview card that mimics the light-mode X UI. Separate documents with their own palette; their backdrops are literals on purpose.
legend.X3: Invoice Studio document preview (contract X3): documents are always light.
legend.X5: Media backdrops (black or dark-ink letterbox behind user video and images): fixed art, not theme (contract X5).
legend.X6: Mode-agnostic or data-semantic colours (contract X6): ink and white shadows, insets and glows, modal scrims, categorical accents.
legend.X7: Always-dark ops consoles (contract X7): AdminPage.jsx and app/admin/control.
legend.X8: Pinned light for v1 (contract X8, extended to the public Studio workbench /dashboard/studio, whose outer shell carries data-theme-scope="light").
legend.W6-A: Never rendered: fallback inside var(--token, literal), or a colour named in a comment.
legend.W6-B: Light content on a fixed fill: white text on the brand gradient, platform chips and photo labels, and white hairlines or washes on dark-styled chrome.
legend.W6-C: Mid-tone saturated status or categorical solid (LED dots, chips, icons), or a data / user colour, with no token inside the closeness threshold. Readable on both modes, so it stays a fixed hue.
legend.W6-E: Intentionally dark console panel (log output, preview well): stays dark in both modes with light text.
